title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
layout_note: One row of four equal panels separated by thin vertical rules: (a) defines a task vector, (b)-(d) apply it (negation, addition, analogy), each as a small vector diagram from one origin circle with its equation above or below and a one-line 'Example: ...' under it.
grouping: Panels are separated only by thin black vertical rules, each titled at its top-left with a letter and a serif name ('a) Task vectors', 'b) Forgetting via negation', 'c) Learning via addition', 'd) Task analogies'). No frames or tints.
shapes_depth: Flat 2-D vector geometry: weights are light-grey circles with black outlines, task vectors are straight coloured arrows from an origin circle, grey dashed lines complete the parallelogram or rectangle constructions; the fine-tuning path in (a) is a grey dashed wiggle. Text and equations are typeset in a serif (Computer Modern) face.
proposed_highlight: The defining panel (a) comes first and carries the only saturated blue arrow; in (c) and (d) the resulting vector τnew is the one saturated purple arrow among pale operand arrows, so each operation's result stands out.
lesson: Draw each arithmetic operation as geometry in one shared vector space - pale operand arrows, a dashed parallelogram, one saturated result arrow - with the equation above it as a caption, one panel per operation.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023'). Candidate domains were llm and vision; the KB has no vision domain, so only llm is kept. elements 'other' = weight-space vector diagrams (arrows from an origin circle).

taxonomy.task: editing pretrained models by adding, negating and combining task vectors
taxonomy.note: family other: model editing in weight space; architecture other: no network drawn, only weights as points and task vectors as arrows; depicts plots = 2-D vector diagrams

insights.structure: Four equal panels in one row: a definition panel followed by three operation panels, separated by thin vertical rules.
insights.data: Weights are grey circles and task vectors are arrows from an origin; each panel's equation is set beside the geometry that draws its terms.
insights.emphasis: In each operation panel the result vector is the one saturated arrow (orange in negation, purple in addition and analogy) among pale operand arrows.
insights.flow: Read panel by panel left to right; inside a panel arrows start at one origin circle and grey dashed lines complete the parallelogram or rectangle that constructs the result.
insights.avoid: An operand's colour changes between panels (τA is pale blue in (c) but pale yellow in (d); τB pink in (c), pale green in (d)) and the result is orange in (b) but purple elsewhere.

arrangement.units: four equal-width unframed panels separated by thin vertical rules, each titled with a letter and a name at the top-left
arrangement.inputs_as: weights as grey circles (θpre, θft) and task vectors as coloured arrows from an origin circle
arrangement.shared: the origin circle (pretrained weights) is redrawn at the base of the arrows in every panel

core.what: each edit drawn as vector geometry in weight space: arrows from one origin circle, a dashed parallelogram or rectangle constructing the sum, the result as the one saturated arrow

relations.form: task vectors are arrows between weight points (grey circles), and sums or differences are drawn as dashed parallelograms and rectangles from one origin
the three operations (negation, addition, analogy) sit in three equal panels side by side after the definition panel, each with its equation and an 'Example:' line in the same places
panel (a) defines τ = θft - θpre with an arrow from θpre to θft beside a dashed wiggly fine-tuning path, and the following panels reuse τ

channels.colour: pale arrows = operand task vectors, a saturated arrow = the vector being defined or produced (blue in (a), orange in (b), purple in (c) and (d)); operand hues are not kept across panels, so colour only separates operand from result within a panel
channels.shape: grey outlined circles = weights (points), straight arrows = task vectors
channels.line: solid arrows = vectors; grey dashed lines = construction lines (parallelogram sides, extension of τ) and in (a) the fine-tuning trajectory
channels.frame: no frames; thin vertical rules divide the panels

quality.strengths: each equation is drawn as its terms - operand arrows, a dashed parallelogram, the result arrow - so the method's arithmetic is visible as geometry; one panel per job (define, then three operations) with identical panel width and the same placement of equation and example; the result arrow is the most saturated mark in each panel
quality.weaknesses: operand colours change between panels (τA pale blue in (c), pale yellow in (d)) and the result is orange in (b) but purple in (c)-(d), so the colour code must be relearned per panel; the pale yellow τA in (d) nearly disappears against white; the 'Example' sentences under each panel use as much height as the diagrams

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
